correctness.rationale: For n>=1, K(n) tests tau((n+k)!)/tau(n!). The exact local ratio R(t)=product_{p^a||t}(V_p(t-1)+a+1)/(V_p(t-1)+1) and estimate R(t)<=exp(S(t)/t) are reconstructed. If t>=2048 is composite, split by largest prime <=sqrt(t) or >sqrt(t), isolating a large prime factor with cofactor a>=2. Consecutive-composite bounds outside cofactors 2,3 are (45/34)^2, (3/2)(15/13)^2, and (9/5)(45/44)^2, all <2. Cofactors 2 and 3 with both complementary large factors prime give product >2. Independent exact integer computation for 2<=m<2048 found 60 double-composite two-step hits: 55 prime-pair and five exceptions 8,15,20,25,34, and the only composite one-step factor m=4. Thus K=1 iff n+1 prime or n=3; the stated K=2 classification exhausts all n, with no infinitude asserted for simultaneous-prime families.
